rules.title: Filter(...) maps to Graph where(...)
caveats: Find's Filter() predicates are evaluated server-side against the index; confirm the equivalent Graph 'where' clause targets the matching indexed field name.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph 'where' clause

rules.title: For(text) maps to Graph query(...)
caveats: Find's For() applies BM25-style free text ranking across all indexed fields; Graph's full text match may rank results differently.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph full text query

rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph 'orderBy' clause

rules.title: ThenBy(...) maps to Graph orderBy(...) secondary sort
caveats: Graph orderBy composes multiple fields in declaration order; verify tie-break order matches the Find ThenBy chain.

rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph 'skip' argument

rules.title: Select(...) projection maps to Graph selection set
rules.graphEquivalent: GraphQL selection set listing only the required fields
caveats: Find's in-memory Select() projection can call arbitrary .NET code; only property-access projections translate directly to a GraphQL selection set.
Confirm the projected properties are exposed on the Graph content type before relying on the generated snippet.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph selection set for simple property projections

rules.title: Track() analytics call has no Graph SDK equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph has no built-in search analytics/tracking pipeline equivalent to Find's Track(). Statistics must be captured with a separate telemetry solution.
rules.suggestedApproach: Emit your own search telemetry: wrap Graph query execution in a search service that logs a structured event per query (term, filters, result count, timestamp, correlation id) and a second event when a result is clicked, then send those to the telemetry sink the solution already uses (ILogger + Application Insights custom events, Optimizely Data Platform, or an events table you own). Rebuild any dashboards or reports as queries over that event stream.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no clean Graph SDK translation; search analytics must be re-implemented separately

rules.title: StaticallyCacheFor(...) maps to Graph client-side caching
rules.graphEquivalent: Cache the GraphQL response in the calling application (for example via IMemoryCache) for an equivalent duration
caveats: Optimizely Graph does not provide Find's built-in response caching; the caching duration and invalidation must be re-implemented in the consuming application.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no built-in Graph SDK equivalent; caching must be implemented by the caller

rules.title: FilterForVisitor() personalization maps to Graph visitor group filtering
caveats: FilterForVisitor() combines access rights, publish status and visitor-group targeting; each dimension must be re-expressed as an explicit Graph 'where' clause against the indexed fields.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to explicit Graph 'where' clauses, but requires manual review

rules.title: GetContentResult() maps to a Graph query execution
caveats: Find returns hydrated IContent instances synchronously; the Graph SDK client is async and returns DTOs shaped by the selection set, not full IContent objects.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}()' can be translated to executing the equivalent Graph query

rules.title: GetFacets(...) maps to Graph facets query
caveats: Find's facet API returns bucket counts computed against the search index; confirm the equivalent Graph facet field is configured as filterable/facetable in the schema.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph facets selection

rules.title: Highlight(...) maps to Graph highlight selection
caveats: Graph's highlighting output format and snippet boundaries differ from Find's; verify the rendered highlight markers match the previous UI expectations.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph highlight selection

rules.title: Range(...) maps to Graph range filter
caveats: Confirm the range boundaries (inclusive/exclusive) match between Find's Range() semantics and the generated Graph 'where' comparison operators.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph range 'where' clause

rules.title: Language(...) maps to Graph language selector
caveats: Find applies language-specific analysis/stemming per query; Graph language filtering is a field match and does not automatically re-run language-aware analysis.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph language 'where' clause, but requires manual review

rules.title: TotalMatching() maps to Graph total count field
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}()' can be translated to the Graph 'totalCount' selection field

rules.title: BestBets(...) has no direct Graph equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph has no built-in editorial promotions/best-bets pinning feature. Pinned results must be re-implemented in application code by merging curated content ahead of the Graph result set.
rules.suggestedApproach: Store the curated promotions yourself - for example a 'Best Bets' CMS block or settings list mapping a search phrase to one or more content references - and resolve it in your search service: look up matches for the current term, load those items, and prepend them to the Graph result set while de-duplicating any that Graph also returned. Remember to exclude the pinned items from the page-size budget so paging stays correct.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no clean Graph SDK translation; editorial best bets must be re-implemented separately

rules.title: DidYouMean()/Autocomplete() have no direct Graph equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph does not provide a built-in spelling-suggestion or autocomplete API equivalent to Find's DidYouMean()/Autocomplete(). A separate suggestion index or third-party service is required.
rules.suggestedApproach: Build a suggestion source of your own: maintain a term dictionary (harvested from indexed titles/keywords or from your logged search terms) and run an edit-distance check - for example a Levenshtein comparison via a library such as Fastenshtein, or a trigram match - against it when a query returns zero or few results, offering the closest term as 'did you mean'. Alternatively delegate to a dedicated service (Azure AI Search suggesters, Algolia) that sits alongside Graph.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no clean Graph SDK translation; suggestion/autocomplete features must be re-implemented separately

rules.title: Autocomplete() has no direct Graph equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph does not provide a built-in autocomplete/type-ahead API equivalent to Find's Autocomplete(). A separate suggestion index or third-party service is required.
rules.suggestedApproach: Implement type-ahead as a lightweight endpoint of your own: for short prefixes, query Graph with a 'startsWith' where clause over an indexed title/keyword field and return just the matched field values, cached per prefix; for richer behaviour, maintain a dedicated suggestion store (a cached in-memory trie built from indexed terms, or a small table of popular search terms captured from your own query telemetry). Debounce on the client and cap the result count.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no clean Graph SDK translation; autocomplete features must be re-implemented separately

rules.title: DistanceFrom(...) geo/spatial filter has no direct Graph equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph does not currently expose geo/spatial distance filtering or sorting equivalent to Find's DistanceFrom(). Location-based search must be re-implemented with a separate geo index or post-filtering in application code.
rules.suggestedApproach: Do the distance work yourself in two stages: narrow the candidate set server-side with a cheap Graph 'where' clause (a bounding box on indexed latitude/longitude fields, or a coarse region/postcode field), then compute exact distances with the haversine formula - or System.Device.Location / NetTopologySuite - and sort and page the results in application code. If geo search is central to the site, consider keeping a purpose-built spatial store (PostGIS, Azure AI Search geo filters, Azure Maps) alongside Graph.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no clean Graph SDK translation; geo/spatial search must be re-implemented separately

rules.title: GetContentResultAsync() maps to an async Graph query execution
caveats: Find returns hydrated IContent instances asynchronously; the Graph SDK client is also async but returns DTOs shaped by the selection set, not full IContent objects.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}()' can be translated to an awaited Graph query execution

rules.title: MoreLikeThis(...) similarity query has no direct Graph equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph does not expose a built-in 'more like this' / content-similarity query. Related-content recommendations must be re-implemented with a separate recommendation service or a hand-rolled 'where' clause approximating similarity on indexed fields (e.g. shared tags/categories).
rules.suggestedApproach: Approximate similarity with explicit signals you already index: take the current item's tags, categories, author or content type, and issue a Graph query for other items sharing them (an OR-composed 'where' clause), excluding the current item, then rank the results in application code by how many signals overlap. Cache the related-items list per content item since it changes rarely. For genuine semantic similarity, delegate to a recommendation or vector-search service and store only the resulting ids.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no clean Graph SDK translation; content-similarity queries must be re-implemented separately

rules.title: Search<T>(CultureInfo) language-scoped query root requires manual review
caveats: Find's Search<T>(CultureInfo) scopes the query root to a single language variant of the index. Graph does not accept a culture argument on the query root; the equivalent language scoping must be expressed as an explicit 'where' clause against the content's language field.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(CultureInfo)' can be translated to a Graph language 'where' clause on the query, but requires manual review

rules.title: RemoveDuplicates() deduplication has no direct Graph equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph queries do not support field-based result deduplication like Find's RemoveDuplicates(). Equivalent behaviour must be implemented by grouping/distinct-ing results in application code after the query executes.
rules.suggestedApproach: De-duplicate after the query: include the field you were de-duplicating on in the selection set, then apply GroupBy(field).Select(g => g.First()) - or DistinctBy on .NET 6+ - to the returned items. Because this shrinks the result set after Graph has already applied skip/limit, over-fetch (request more items than the page size) and page the de-duplicated list in application code, or better, fix the duplication at its source so the index holds one entry per logical item.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no clean Graph SDK translation; result deduplication must be re-implemented separately

rules.title: MinScore(...) relevance threshold has no direct Graph equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph does not expose the raw relevance score used by Find's MinScore()/RemoveMatchScoreThreshold(), so a query cannot filter on it directly. Consider filtering results in application code, or re-approximating the cutoff with an explicit 'where' clause on indexed fields.
rules.suggestedApproach: Replace the score cutoff with an explicit quality rule. In most cases the intent is 'hide weak matches', which is better expressed as a stricter 'where' clause (require the term in a title/keyword field rather than anywhere in the body) or simply as a smaller result limit. If you need a relative cutoff, apply it in application code using a signal you control - for example drop results below a computed relevance score of your own, or below a fraction of the top result's score - rather than Graph's internal ranking.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no clean Graph SDK translation; relevance-score thresholds must be re-implemented separately

rules.title: MatchContained(...) content-tree ancestor filter maps to Graph ancestor 'where' clause
caveats: Find's MatchContained() filters by the content tree ancestor path stored in its index. Graph exposes ancestor/parent information with a different field name and shape, so confirm the equivalent 'where' clause targets the correct Graph ancestor field before relying on the generated snippet.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph ancestor 'where' clause, but requires manual review

rules.title: ForVisitorGroup(...) personalization maps to Graph visitor group filtering
caveats: ForVisitorGroup() scopes results to a specific visitor group's personalization rules. Each targeting dimension must be re-expressed as an explicit Graph 'where' clause against the indexed fields, the same way as the parameterless FilterForVisitor() overload (see OGM011).
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to explicit Graph 'where' clauses, but requires manual review

rules.title: AverageOf/SumOf/MaximumOf/MinimumOf statistical aggregation has no direct Graph equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph does not expose server-side numeric aggregation (average/sum/min/max) over a field the way Find's AverageOf()/SumOf()/MaximumOf()/MinimumOf() do. Equivalent aggregates must be computed in application code after retrieving the matching results, or via a separate reporting/analytics data store.
rules.suggestedApproach: Compute the aggregate yourself. For small result sets, project just the numeric field into the Graph selection set and use LINQ (Average/Sum/Max/Min) over the returned items, paging through all matches first so the figure is not computed from a single page. Where the aggregate spans a large or unbounded set, or drives reporting, source it from the system of record instead - a SQL query, a Commerce/CMS API, or a nightly-computed figure cached in your own store - rather than from the search index.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' has no clean Graph SDK translation; numeric aggregation must be re-implemented separately

rules.title: AverageOf/SumOf/MaximumOf/MinimumOf statistical aggregation has no direct Graph equivalent
caveats: Optimizely Graph does not expose server-side numeric aggregation (average/sum/min/max) over a field the way Find's AverageOf()/SumOf()/MaximumOf()/MinimumOf() do. Equivalent aggregates must be computed in application code after retrieving the matching results, or via a separate reporting/analytics data store.
rules.suggestedApproach: Compute the aggregate yourself. A max/min over an indexed field is often better expressed as an ordered query - request the single top result with an 'orderBy' on that field and a limit of 1 - which avoids fetching the whole set. Where that is not possible, project the field into the selection set and use LINQ over all matching items, or source the figure from the system of record (SQL, a Commerce/CMS API, or a cached precomputed value) rather than from the search index.

rules.title: Fuzzy(...) fuzzy-matching query modifier maps to Graph fuzzy search with different semantics
caveats: Find's Fuzzy() uses a similarity/edit-distance threshold that does not map one-to-one onto Graph's fuzzy-matching behavior. Verify result quality against representative queries after migrating, since Graph may return different matches for the same threshold value.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph fuzzy 'where' clause, but requires manual review

rules.title: TermsFacetFor/RangeFacetFor facet-builder detail requires manual review
caveats: Find's TermsFacetFor()/RangeFacetFor() configure facet bucket size and range boundaries directly on the query builder. Graph exposes facets in its GraphQL selection set instead, with a different mechanism for controlling bucket count and range boundaries, so the configuration must be re-expressed there.
rules.messageFormat: Find '{0}(...)' can be translated to a Graph facets selection, but requires manual review
